problem_statement: Ibaliqbal/grid-layout-transition is a static Codrops gallery demo (a GSAP Flip powered grid of local WebP image tiles) whose Default page (index.html) ships a shared black frame masthead (the #Grid Layout Transition with #GSAP title, the Article / All demos / GitHub links and the five 50 / 75 / 100 / 125 / 150 grid-size controls) driving the grid through several layout modes, plus a companion Filter + Stagger page (index2.html) that reuses the same masthead. A first-time visitor is dropped into the raw controls with no guided reading order. Add a shared on-page Layout Flow Guide (nav.flowguide) into the frame masthead of BOTH pages: a labeled reading order over the demo's real layout modes that wires its step controls to the demo's own grid-size buttons (so it drives the existing GSAP Flip transition rather than adding a parallel control surface) and keeps a live 'Current view' readout in sync with the active mode. Compose it from the shared frame chrome, keep every page free of horizontal overflow on mobile, and keep the existing gallery, controls and Filter + Stagger route intact.
required_content: Add an on-page Layout Flow Guide strip (nav.flowguide) into the shared frame masthead with a labeled 'Layout Flow Guide' header and at least five ordered steps.
Label the steps as a reading order over the demo's real layout modes: 01 Default 75% grid, 02 Dense 50% scan, 03 Full 100% read, 04 Wide 150% focus, 05 Filter + Stagger route.
Place the same Layout Flow Guide in the masthead of BOTH the Default page (index.html) and the Filter + Stagger route page (index2.html) so the guide is a consistent cross-page fixture.

Wire the guide's step controls to the demo's own grid-size buttons (data-guide-size) so the guide drives the existing GSAP Flip transition, and keep a live 'Current view: ...' readout in sync with the mode the visitor last picked.
Compose the guide from the shared frame chrome and thin-border compact rhythm so it is visually indistinguishable in system from the rest of the masthead.
Keep every page free of horizontal overflow on desktop, tablet and at 390px mobile, and keep the existing gallery and controls intact.
design_constraints: Build the Layout Flow Guide from the shared frame masthead chrome and thin-border button style, not a standalone page with bespoke inline markup.

Preserve the shared frame masthead layout, the demo nav and the uppercase thin-border compact control spacing/typography used across both pages; keep the guide on-palette (dark surface, gray text, 1px borders) so it is visually consistent with the existing style.
Keep the guide free of horizontal overflow on mobile / responsive widths (the fixed-width row must wrap rather than push the page wider than the viewport).
The guide's 'Current view' readout must reflect the grid layout mode the visitor last selected via the guide button (a stale readout that never updates is a defect).
Treat this as a flow-level experience add: the guide must appear on both pages and must drive the demo's existing grid-size control (the WebP image grid) rather than duplicating it.
state_constraints: desktop_flow_guide verifies the Layout Flow Guide renders in the frame masthead: the nav.flowguide carries a 'Layout Flow Guide' label and the five ordered step controls within the shared frame chrome.
mobile_flow_guide / tablet_flow_guide verify the guide holds the same design system with no horizontal overflow at 390px / tablet widths.
desktop_route_guide / mobile_route_guide verify the SAME guide is present on the Filter + Stagger route page (index2.html).
desktop_wide_focus verifies that clicking the '04 Wide 150% focus' step drives the grid AND re-syncs the 'Current view' readout to 'Current view: Wide 150% focus'.

change_completion: The Layout Flow Guide exists in the frame masthead of both pages with a 'Layout Flow Guide' label and at least five ordered step labels covering the demo's real grid layout modes.
The guide's step buttons drive the demo's own data-guide-size grid controls and the 'Current view' readout stays in sync with the last-picked mode.
design_consistency: The guide is composed from the shared frame chrome (dark surface, gray text, 1px thin borders, uppercase typography) so its style matches the existing masthead.
The same guide appears with identical visual treatment on both the Default page and the Filter + Stagger route page.
responsive: On mobile (390px) the guide's step row wraps and introduces no horizontal overflow.
The guide keeps its layout and spacing legible across desktop, tablet and mobile / responsive widths.
regression: The existing image gallery, grid-size controls and GSAP Flip transitions remain intact and keep working after the guide is added.
The frame masthead title, demo nav and Filter + Stagger route remain unchanged and functional.

author_notes: L4 hardened: the bad solution fails FOUR orthogonal gates — no_horizontal_overflow (D6, the fixed-width nowrap flowguide row overflows mobile even behind an overflow-x:hidden mask), visual_regression (D3, the guide is restyled into an off-palette bright slab), dom_assertions (D2 cross-PAGE, the guide is dropped from the Filter + Stagger route page) and interaction_assertions (D4, clicking a step drives the grid but never re-syncs the 'Current view' readout). The baseline reproduces only the layout defect (D6/D3/D2) and keeps the readout wired, so it passes D4 — the four discriminators are on independent axes.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Unused Ibaliqbal grid-layout-transition static Codrops GSAP-Flip gallery demo whose Default page ships a consistent product design system (a shared black frame masthead, an uppercase thin-border control rhythm and the 50/75/100/125/150 grid-size controls); an experience_continuity Consistency task to ADD an on-page Layout Flow Guide reading-order strip that must conform to that existing design system (driving the demo's own grid controls) without diverging into an off-system one-off or stripping the guide's visible step labels.
